generatedProse.concept-context: For a sport student, this is one habit across every coaching placement, lab session and club role. Before a placement with a team or in a physiology lab you set aims, maybe to run a fitness test well or learn how a coach plans a session. While there you act and seek feedback; afterwards you evidence what you learned. Each experience then improves how you aim at the next.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students take on a series of placements: first a community coaching role, then support work with a strength and conditioning team. One turns up, follows instructions, and later writes a plain list of sessions attended. The other sets aims, volunteers to lead a drill, asks the coach for feedback, and records what each placement taught about coaching and testing. By the second placement, that student is given real responsibility and can show exactly what they learned.
generatedProse.summary: In sport, making the most of placements is one continuing practice, not a single effort on your best week. You aim, act and evidence on each coaching, lab or club experience, and carry what you learn into the next. Over your degree, that habit builds the practical skills and the evidence that coaching and sport-science roles ask for.

check.body: A student sets aims for a placement, takes initiative and seeks feedback throughout, then evidences what they learned. They carry one lesson into their next placement, which goes better. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That making the most of experience works as one continuing practice, run across placement after placement.
_items.feedback: Yes. The whole loop ran, and carrying it forward improved the next placement.

_items.text: That the first placement was a better opportunity than most.
_items.feedback: The point is not the placement itself. It is the practice the student ran on it.

_items.text: That evidencing learning is the only part that matters.
_items.feedback: Evidencing is one part. Aiming and acting came first and made the evidence possible.

_items.text: That this only works for students who are naturally confident.
_items.feedback: The practice helped this student whatever their starting point. It is the habit, not the personality.
